name: Aspic Jelly
author: Fannie Merritt Farmer (1896)

ingredients.item: Carrot│2 tbsp each, cut into cubes
1 quart White Stock for vegetables and
1 quart Brown Stock for dark meat

steps: Aspic jelly is always made with meat stock, and is principally used in elaborate entrées where fish, chicken, game, or vegetables are to be served moulded in jelly.
In making Aspic Jelly, use as much liquid as the pan which is to contain moulded dish will hold.
Put vegetables, seasonings, and wine (except two tablespoons) in a saucepan; cook eight minutes, and strain, reserving liquid.
Add gelatine to stock, then add lemon juice.
Heat to boiling-point and add strained liquid.
Beat whites of eggs slightly, add two tablespoons wine, and dilute with one cup hot mixture.
Add slowly to remaining mixture, stirring constantly until boiling-point is reached.
Place on back of range and let stand thirty minutes.
Strain through a double cheese-cloth placed over a fine wire strainer, or through a jelly bag.

culture.text: From The Boston Cooking-School Cook Book (1896) by Fannie Merritt Farmer. It popularized level, standardized measurements (cups and spoons) in American home kitchens, and stayed one of the best-selling cookbooks in the United States for decades.
